parts.problem_md:
A cone has height 15 cm and a base of radius 9 cm.

A smaller cone is cut off the top to form a frustum of height 11 cm.

![Diagram of a frustum, showing its formation from a cone. Includes measurements: diameter 9 cm, height 15 cm, labelled "Frustum".](assets/001-diagram-of-a-frustum-showing-its-formation-from-.png)

Find the exact volume of the frustum.
parts.solution_md:
> *The volume of the frustum is equal to the volume of the large cone, subtract the volume of the smaller cone that has been removed*

> *The formula for the volume of a cone is given by *$V=\frac{1}{3}πr^{2}h$

> *Find the volume of the larger cone *$( V_{L} )$

$V_{L} = 1 \frac{1}{3} \pi ( 9^{2} ) ( 15 )
V_{L} = 405 \pi$

**[M1 A1]**

> *The smaller cone has a height of 15-11=4 cm*

> *The radius of the smaller cone is not known yet, but you can use similarity to find it*

> *Consider a cross section of the large cone and the small cone. You know the height of the small cone (4), the height of the large cone (15) and the radius of the large cone (9)*

![Two right-angled triangles; small one with height 4 cm, base r cm, large one with height 15 cm, base 9 cm; sides are proportional.](assets/002-two-right-angled-triangles-small-one-with-height.png)

> *The triangles are similar; there is a constant scale factor for the side lengths*

$\begin{gathered} \frac{4}{15} & = \frac{r}{9} \\ \frac{4}{15} \times 9 & = r \\ 2.4 & = r \end{gathered}$

**[M1]**

> *Find the volume of the smaller cone *$( V_{S} )$

$V_{S} = 1 \frac{1}{3} \pi ( 2.4 )^{2} ( 4 )
V_{S} = \frac{192}{25} \pi$

**[A1]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Alternatively, you could use a volume scale factor to find the smaller cone's volume:
> 
> $V_{S} = ( \frac{4}{15} )^{3} \times V_{L}$

> *The volume of the frustum is the volume of the larger cone subtract the volume of the smaller cone*

$V=V_{L}-V_{S}=405π-\frac{192}{25}π$

**[M1]**

$\frac{9933}{25}π$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Use of $V=\frac{1}{3}πr^{2}h$.
> 
> **A1**: Finding the volume of the larger cone. Can be implied by later working.
> 
> **M1**: Evidence of using similarity. Either to find the unknown radius or using a volume scale factor $( \frac{4}{15} )^{3}$.
> 
> **A1**: Finding the volume of the smaller cone. Can be implied by later working.
> 
> **M1**: Method to find the volume of the frustum.
> 
> **A1**: Correct final answer or equivalent. Must be exact as specified in the question.

parts.problem_md:
The area of triangle *ADX* is 36 cm<sup>2</sup> and the area of triangle *BCX* is 65.61 cm<sup>2</sup>. 
*AX* = 8.6 cm and *DX* = 7.2 cm. Find *BX*.

*BX* = .................................. cm
parts.solution_md:
> *First find the **area** (2D) scale factor.*

$\frac{65.61}{36}=1.8225$

> *This is the area scale factor **from** triangle **ADX** **to** triangle **BCX**. *
*We can now find the linear (1D) scale factor by square rooting.*

$\sqrt{1.8225}=1.35$

**[1]**

> *BX** is similar to **AX** so*

$BX=8.6\times1.35=11.61$

**[1]**

**BX**** = 11.61 cm*** ***[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Two containers are mathematically similar. 
The surface area of the larger container is 226 cm<sup>2</sup> and the surface area of the smaller container is 94 cm<sup>2</sup>. 
The volume of the larger container is 680 cm<sup>3</sup>.

Find the volume of the smaller container.

........................................... cm<sup>3</sup>
parts.solution_md:
*If two shapes are mathematically similar, their length, area and volume scale factors are **k**, **k*<sup>*2*</sup>* and **k*<sup>*3*</sup> 
*Find the area scale factor, from small-to-large (by dividing the large area by the small area)* * *

$k^{2}=\frac{226}{94}$ * *

*Find the length scale factor, **k**, by square-rooting both sides* * *

$k=\sqrt{\frac{226}{94}}$

**[1]**

*Find the volume scale factor, **k*<sup>*3*</sup>*, by cubing **k* * *

$k ^{3} = ( \sqrt{\frac{226}{94}} ) ^{3}$ * *

*This scale factor is how much bigger the larger container is compared to the smaller container* * *

*the larger volume, 680 cm**<sup>3</sup>**, is *$( \sqrt{\frac{226}{94}} ) ^{3}$* times bigger than the smaller volume* * *

*Find the smaller volume, by dividing the large volume by *$( \sqrt{\frac{226}{94}} ) ^{3}$ * *

*smaller volume = *$\frac{680}{open} \text{parentheses} \sqrt{\frac{226}{94}} ) ^{3}$

**[1]**

> *Use a calculator to find this value, giving your answer to 3 significant figures*

**182 cm**<sup>**3**</sup>** ****[1]**

equations.alt: k equals square root of 226 over 94 end root

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows two water towers in Kuwait.

![q7-paper1hr-jan2019-edexcel-igcse-maths](assets/004-q7-paper1hr-jan2019-edexcel-igcse-maths.png)

The real height of tower $A$ is $187m$. 
The real height of tower $B$ is $147m$.

Ahmed makes a scale model of both towers.

The height of tower $A$ on the scale model is $90\mathrm{cm}$.

Work out the height of tower $B$ on the scale model. Give your answer correct to the nearest centimetre.
parts.solution_md:
> *The height of model **A** and the height of model **B** are corresponding lengths in similar shapes so find **k, **the scale factor, using**  *$\begin{array}{rcl} k = \frac{second \text{corresponding} length}{first \text{corresponding} length} \end{array}$

> *Method 1*

> *The height of model **B** is smaller than the height of model **A**. **To go from the big shape to the small shape, put the small length on top in the fraction so that **k** will be smaller than 1*

$\begin{gathered} k & = \frac{height B}{height A} = \frac{147}{187} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Find the height of model **B** by multiplying the height of model **A** by **k **(notice that **k** < 1 so multiplying by **k** will make the length smaller)*

$\begin{gathered} \text{height} B & = k [ \text{height} A ] = \frac{147}{187} \times 90 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} = 70.7486631... \end{gathered}$

> *This answer is already in centimetres but give the final answer to the nearest centimetre as requested in the question*

**71 cm**** ****[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *Finding **k **using**  *$\begin{array}{rcl} k = \frac{second \text{corresponding} length}{first \text{corresponding} length} \end{array}$*, if you put the larger length on top of the fraction then;*

$\begin{gathered} k & = \frac{height A}{height B} = \frac{187}{147} \end{gathered}$

> *Notice that **k** > 1 so multiplying by **k** will make the length bigger- but in going from the height of model **A** to the height of model of **B**, we want to go from a longer length to a smaller length. So divide by **k **instead*

$\begin{gathered} \text{height} B & = \text{height} A \div k = 90 \div \frac{187}{147} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{gathered} = 70.7486631... \end{gathered}$

> *This answer is already in centimetres but give the final answer to the nearest centimetre as requested in the question*

**71 cm**** ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows two cylinders, $A$ and $B$

![q6-paper2h-june2018-edexcel-igcse-maths](assets/005-q6-paper2h-june2018-edexcel-igcse-maths.png)

Cylinder $A$ has height 1.6 m and radius 0.56 m.

Cylinder $B$ is mathematically similar to cylinder $A$.
The height of cylinder $B$ is 0.6 m. 
Work out the radius of cylinder $B$.

....................................................... m
parts.solution_md:
> *The radius of **A** and the radius of **B** are corresponding lengths in similar shapes so find **k, **the scale factor, using**  *$\begin{array}{rcl} k = \frac{second \text{corresponding} length}{first \text{corresponding} length} \end{array}$

> *Method 1*

> *The radius of **B** is smaller than the radius of **A**. **To go from the big shape to the small shape, put the small length on top in the fraction so that **k** will be smaller than 1*

$\begin{gathered} k & = \frac{height B}{height A} = \frac{0.6}{1.6} = \frac{3}{8} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Find radius of **B** by multiplying the radius of **A** by **k **(notice that **k** < 1 so multiplying by **k** will make the length smaller)*

$\begin{gathered} \text{radius} B & = k [ \text{radius} A ] = \frac{3}{8} \times 0.56 \end{gathered}$

**0.21 m**** ****[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *Finding **k **using**  *$\begin{array}{rcl} k = \frac{second \text{corresponding} length}{first \text{corresponding} length} \end{array}$*, if you put the larger length on top of the fraction then;*

$\begin{gathered} k & = \frac{height A}{height B} = \frac{1.6}{0.6} = \frac{8}{3} \end{gathered}$

> *Notice that **k** > 1 so multiplying by **k** will make the length bigger- but in going from the radius of **A** to the radius of **B**, we want to go from a longer length to a smaller length. So divide by **k **instead*

$\begin{gathered} \text{radius} B & = \text{radius} A \div k = 0.56 \div \frac{3}{8} \end{gathered}$

**0.21 m**** ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
A model of a statue has a height of 4cm.
The volume of the model is 12 cm<sup>3</sup>. 
The volume of the statue is 40 500 cm<sup>3</sup>.

Calculate the height of the statue.

............................................ cm
parts.solution_md:
> *The statue and the model are similar so there will exist a value of **k **such that the volume of the statue (**V*<sub>*S*</sub>*) = **k*<sup>*3 *</sup>*× **volume of the model (**V*<sub>*M*</sub>*).*

> *Form an equation using the two volumes.*

$\begin{gathered} V_{S} & = k^{3} V_{M} \\ 40 500 & = 12 k^{3} \end{gathered}$

> *Solve to find *$k$*.*

$\begin{gathered} k^{3} & = \frac{40 500}{12} = 3375 \\ k & = \sqrt[3]{3375} = 15 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *The same proportions will apply to the height of the model and the statue, however height is one dimension so the formula *$\begin{gathered} h_{S} & = k ( h_{M} ) \end{gathered}$* is used.*

$\begin{gathered} h_{S} & = 4 ( h_{M} ) \\ = ( 4 ) ( 15 ) \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

**The height of the statue is 60 cm ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:

*PQR* is a triangle.

*RQ* is parallel to *TU*.

Explain why triangle *PQR* is similar to triangle *PUT*. Give a reason for each statement you make.
parts.solution_md:
> *Similar triangles have three equal angles. *
*Identify any corresponding angles that are equal between triangles **PQR**  and **PUT**.*

> *The lines **TU **and **RQ **are parallel. *
*In parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal.*

> *The statement that if three corresponding angles between two triangles are equal then the two triangles are similar must be made.*

**Final answer:** **Angle ****TPU****  = angle ****RPQ****  as they are a common angle. **
**Angle ****PTU****  = angle ****PRQ ****as they are corresponding angles on parallel lines. **
**Angle ****PUT****  = angle ****PQR ****as they are corresponding angles on parallel lines.**** **

**A****t least two of the three statements given, with reasons ****[2]**

** All three angles are the same so the triangles are similar. *** *
**Explanation of similar triangles ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

PQR is a triangle. T is a point on PR and U is a point on PQ. RQ is parallel to TU.

*PT* : *TR* = 4 : 3

i) Find the ratio *PU* : *PQ*.

...................... : ...................... [1]

ii) The area of triangle *PUT* is 20cm<sup>2</sup>. Find the area of the quadrilateral *QRTU*.

.......................................... cm<sup>2</sup> [3]
parts.solution_md:
i) *The triangles are similar, so there will exist a constant, **k, **such that **PU **:** UQ **= **k **(**PT **: TR).   Adding the values to the diagram may help.*

![cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz3-q5bii-working](assets/007-cie-igcse-2020-oct-nov-p4-tz3-q5bii-working.png)

$PU:UQ=4k:3k$

> *  PQ** = **PU **+** UQ, **so the ratio** PU : PQ **will be equal to the ratio **PU **: (**PU + UQ**).*

> * *

$\begin{gathered} P U : ( P U + U Q ) & = 4 k : ( 4 k + 3 k ) \\ P U : P Q & = 4 k : 7 k \end{gathered}$

> * *

> *Simplify by dividing both sides by **k.*

> * *

**4 : 7**** [1]**

ii) *For two lengths, **A** and **B**  to be mathematically similar, there must be a value of **k** such that **A **= **kB. *

> *For two areas, **A** and **B**  to be mathematically similar, there must be a value of **k** such that **A **= **k*<sup>*2*</sup>*B.*

> *The area of quadrilateral **QRTU  **= area of triangle **PQR **- area of triangle **PUT.** Find the area of triangle **PQR **first.*

> *If the length **PU **=** kPQ  **for some value of **k**, then area** PUT **= **k*<sup>*2*</sup>*(area **PQR**).*

> *Use the ratio **PU **: **PQ **= 4 : 7 to find the value of** k such that PU **=** kPQ .*

$\begin{gathered} 7 P U & = 4 P Q \\ P U & = \frac{4 P Q}{7} \\ P U & = \frac{4}{7} P Q \\ k & = \frac{4}{7} \end{gathered}$

> *The area of triangle **PQR **= **k*<sup>*2*</sup>*(area **PUT**). *

> *Use this value of **k** with the area of triangle **PUT ** to find the area of triangle **PQR.** Remember to use **k*<sup>*2  *</sup>*in the formula as we are working with area.*

`| Area _ P U T end _ | = k ^2 x Area _ P Q R end _ | | 20 | = ( 4 / 7 ) ^2 x Area _ P Q R end _ | | Area _ P Q R end _ | = ( 20)/( ( 4 / 7 ) ^2) | | _ = 61.25 | |`

*  **Correct scale factor squared*** ****[1]  **

*Correct formula*** ****[1]**

> *Find the area of quadrilateral **QRTU  **using the area of triangle **PQR **minus the area of triangle **PUT.*

*Area of quadrilateral*** QRTU  ***= 61.25 - 20*

**Area = 41.25 cm**<sup>**2  **</sup>**[1]**

parts.problem_md:
![cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-3-p2-q25b](assets/008-cie-igcse-2018-may-jun-3-p2-q25b.png)

The diagram shows two glasses which are mathematically similar. 
The larger glass has a capacity of 0.5 litres and the smaller glass has a capacity of 0.25 litres. 
The height of the larger glass is 13 cm.

Calculate the height of the smaller glass.

........................................... cm
parts.solution_md:
> *For similar shapes, if the scale factor of enlargement for lengths is *$k$*, then the capacity scale factor is *$k^{3}$* (capacity is equivalent to volume). In this example, the volume scale factor is *

$k^{3}=\frac{0.5}{0.25}=2$

> *Therefore the length scale factor is the cube root of 2.*

$k = \sqrt[3]{2}$

**[1]**

> *The height of the larger glass is 13 cm. To get get the height of the smaller glass we need to divide by the length scale factor. *
*A common mistake here is to multiply rather than divide, but this will give you a larger height- remember we're finding the height of the smaller glass.*

$\begin{gathered} h = 13 \div \sqrt[3]{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

$\begin{array}{rcl} = 10.31810684... \end{array}$

> *Round your answer to at least 3 significant figures.*

$h=10.3$** [1]**
**Check that your answer is a smaller height than 13 cm**

equations.alt: k cubed equals fraction numerator 0.5 over denominator 0.25 end fraction equals 2
bold italic h bold equals bold 10 bold. bold 3

parts.problem_md:
![screenshot-2023-05-26-at-4-54-15-pm](assets/009-screenshot-2023-05-26-at-4-54-15-pm.png)

*ABC* and *EDC* are straight lines. 
*EA* is parallel to *DB*.

*EC* = 8.1 cm.
*DC* = 5.4 cm. 
*DB* = 2.6 cm,

Work out the length of *AE*.
parts.solution_md:
> *All of the corresponding angles in the triangles **AEC **and **BDC **are the same, as angle **BCD** is in both triangles, and the other angles are corresponding angles on parallel lines. *

*Triangles ***AEC ***and ***BDC ***are similar*

> *The triangles are similar so there will exist a value of **k **such that  *$\begin{gathered} A E & = k B D \end{gathered}$*, *$\begin{gathered} C D & = k C E \end{gathered}$* and *$\begin{gathered} B C & = k A C \end{gathered}$*. *
*k **is known as the scale factor.*

> *It may help to draw the two triangles out separately next to each other.*

![4-8-edexcel-gcse-mq6](assets/010-4-8-edexcel-gcse-mq6.png)

> *Form an equation using the two known sides of the triangle.*

$\begin{gathered} C E & = k C D \end{gathered}$

> *Substitute the values of *$CE$* and *$CD$* into the equation and solve to find *$k$*.*

$\begin{gathered} 8.1 & = 5.4 k \\ k & = \frac{8.1}{5.4} = \frac{3}{2} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute into *$\begin{gathered} A E & = k B D \end{gathered}$*.*

$\begin{gathered} A E & = k B D \\ x & = ( \frac{3}{2} ) ( 2.6 ) \end{gathered}$

$AE=3.9$** cm**** ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Two mathematically similar containers have heights of 30 cm and 75 cm. 
The larger container has a capacity of 5.5 litres.

Calculate the capacity of the smaller container.
Give your answer in millilitres.

............................................... ml
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the length scale factor (LSF) by dividing the height of the larger cone by the height of the smaller cone.*

$\mathrm{LSF}=\frac{75}{30}=2.5$

> *The volume scale factor (VSF), is the cube of the LSF.*

$\mathrm{VSF}=\mathrm{LSF}^{3}$

> *Find the VSF by cubing the LSF.*

$\mathrm{VSF}=2.5^{3}$

$\mathrm{VSF}=15.625$

**[1]**

> *Find the volume of the smaller container by dividing the volume of the larger container by the VSF.*

$5.5\div15.625=0.352$

> *Convert the value from litres into ml by multiplying by 1000.*

$0.352\times1000$

**[1]**

$352$** ml** **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Two cones are mathematically similar. 
The total surface area of the smaller cone is 80 cm<sup>2</sup>. The total surface area of the larger cone is 180 cm<sup>2</sup>. The volume of the smaller cone is 168 cm<sup>3</sup>.

Calculate the volume of the larger cone.

............................................. cm<sup>3</sup>
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the area scale factor (ASF) by dividing the area of the larger cone by the area of the smaller cone.*

$\mathrm{ASF}=\frac{180}{80}=2.25$

*Method 1* 
*The ratio of radii (lengths) is 1 : 2 so the ratio of volumes is 1*<sup>*3*</sup>* : 2*<sup>*3*</sup>

The diagram shows two shapes that are mathematically similar. 
The smaller shape has area 52.5 cm<sup>2</sup> and the larger shape has area 134.4 cm<sup>2</sup>.

Calculate the value of $m$.

$m=$................................................
parts.solution_md:
> *Find the area scale factor needed by dividing the area of the larger shape by the area of the smaller shape. *

$\frac{134.4}{52.5}=2.56$

> *The area scale factor is the square of the length scale factor. Square root the area scale factor to find the scale factor between the lengths.*

$\sqrt{2.56}=1.6$

**[1]**

> *As we are finding a missing length on the smaller shape we need to divide the length on the larger shape by the length scale factor.*

$m=\frac{8}{1.6}$

**[1]**

$m=5$* ***[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Manjeet has two mathematically similar bottles in her bathroom. 
The large bottle holds 1.35 litres and is 29.7 cm high. The small bottle holds 0.4 litres.

Calculate the height of the small bottle.

............................................ cm
parts.solution_md:
> *First we need to find the volume (3D) scale factor as we know the volume of both the large and small bottles. *
*As we are trying to find the height of the small bottle, we want the scale factor to be **"from** large **to** small".*

*Volume scale factor *$=\frac{0.4}{1.35}=\frac{8}{27}$

> *Do not round this! *
*Height is a linear (1D) measurement so the height scale factor will be the cube root of the volume scale factor.*

$\sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{27}} = \frac{2}{3}$

**[1]**

> *Now we can find the height of the small bottle by multiplying the height of the large bottle by the linear scale factor.*

$29.7\times\frac{2}{3}=\frac{99}{5}=19.8$

** [1]**

**19.8 cm ****[1]**

parts.problem_md:
Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $PQR$.

![cie-igcse-q12-similar-triangles](assets/025-cie-igcse-q12-similar-triangles.png)

Find $PQ$.

$PQ=$ ......................................... cm
parts.solution_md:
> *The triangles are similar so there will exist a value of **k **such that  *$\begin{gathered} P Q & = k A B \end{gathered}$* and *$\begin{array}{rcl} P R & = k A C \end{array}$*.*

> *Form an equation using the two known sides of the triangle.*

$\begin{gathered} P R & = k A C \end{gathered}$

> *Substitute the values of *$PR$* and *$AC$* into the equation and solve to find *$k$*.*

$\begin{gathered} 21.7 & = 12.4 k \\ k & = \frac{21.7}{12.4} = 1.75 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute into *$\begin{gathered} P Q & = k A B \end{gathered}$*.*

$\begin{gathered} P Q & = k A B \\ P Q & = ( 1.75 ) ( 5.2 ) \end{gathered}$

$PQ=9.1$** cm**** ****[1]**
